mainTopic: Feeding a wife whose husband went overseas: שמואל's defenses, the final הלכה like רב, and the new משנה about a provider who fed her
overview: The גמרא is in the middle of the argument between רב and שמואל about a wife whose husband went overseas: does בית דין give her food from his property? It first finishes a side dispute about whether she also gets צדקה or תכשיט. Then it brings three sources against שמואל: a יבמה whose יבם ran away, a woman who comes back from overseas and says her husband died or divorced her, and a ממאנת. שמואל answers each one. Either the husband was reported dead, or his two worries (that he left her money, or told her to live on her earnings) do not apply. Next, רב דימי and רבין report real court cases before רבי and רבי ישמעאל, with opposite versions of who gave her food. The גמרא rules like רב: we give food to a married woman whose husband went away. It adds rulings that a wife may give up her food and keep her earnings, and that white and black glazed vessels without cracks are permitted while green ones are forbidden. A new משנה follows: someone fed a wife while her husband was overseas. חנן says the provider lost his money, and the בני כהנים גדולים say he swears and collects. The גמרא then begins quoting a משנה from נדרים about a מודר הנאה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the dispute over charity versus jewelry
steps.stepSummary: The view that בית דין gives no צדקה from the absent husband's property still agrees that it gives her תכשיט, because he would not want her to look shabby.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The one who says no jewelry certainly says no] charity. The one who says no charity agrees that we do give her jewelry, because the husband would not want her to look degraded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes showing how far each side of the dispute goes. The one who says 'no צדקה' still allows תכשיט for the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking צדקה out of a man's property without his knowledge is not allowed, so one view says בית דין will not do it. But jewelry is for the wife's own dignity, and we assume a husband wants that. So this view gives her תכשיט even though it does not give צדקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Charity given from the husband's property
Jewelry or ornaments for the wife
We give
He is not pleased with it
She would be degraded or look shabby

phrases.english: [all the more so, she is not given] charity.
The one who said [she is not given] charity —
but jewelry, we do give her,
since he would not be happy for her to be degraded.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר צְדָקָה — אֲבָל תַּכְשִׁיט יָהֲבִינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes defining the two sides of the dispute that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The view that withholds צדקה still gives the wife תכשיט from the husband's property, because a husband does not want his wife degraded.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a יבמה that seems to contradict שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if a יבם is ordered by בית דין and runs away, the יבמה is fed from his property. This seems to go against שמואל, who will not feed an absent husband's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A יבמה is fed from her late husband's property for the first three months. After that she is not fed from her husband's property or from the יבם's. If the יבם stood in court and ran away, she is fed from the יבם's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge שמואל. If בית דין feeds a woman from an absent יבם's property, it should surely feed a wife from an absent husband's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבם owes a יבמה less than a husband owes his wife. Yet the ברייתא feeds her from his property while he is away. So it seems we should not worry, as שמואל does, that the absent man already arranged her support.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a source as a proof or challenge
A widow whose husband died childless, waiting for יבום or חליצה
The late husband's brother
She is fed or supported
He stood in court

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never mentions שמואל. The challenge is unspoken: the גמרא expects you to see that feeding her from an absent יבם's property clashes with שמואל's view.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The widow waiting for her brother-in-law —
for the first three months
is fed from her husband's property;
from then on,
she is not fed, not from her husband's property
and not from the brother-in-law's.
If he stood in court and ran away —
phrases.notes: 'He' is the יבם. בית דין ruled against him, and he fled to avoid it.

phrases.english: she is fed from the brother-in-law's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main question of שמואל's ruling about an absent husband and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that בית דין does not feed the wife of a man who went overseas
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בית דין feeds a יבמה from an absent יבם's property, even though he owes her less than a husband does, then surely it should feed a wife from her absent husband's property.

steps.title: שמואל: neither of my worries applies to a יבם
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that his two reasons for not feeding a wife (hidden money, or permission to use her earnings) do not apply to a יבם and יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל can say to you: What is there to worry about here? If we worry he left her bundles of money, he is not close enough to her to do that. If we worry he told her to live off her earnings, her earnings do not belong to him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל defends himself. He shows that the reasons behind his ruling about a husband do not fit the case of a יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל held back food from the wife for two reasons. Maybe the husband left her צררי, or maybe he told her to use her מעשה ידיה. A יבם is not close enough to the woman to leave her money, and her earnings do not belong to him to give away, so the ברייתא can feed her without contradicting שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you, introducing a defense
Should we worry
Bundles of money left with her
Her earnings from her work
Bound or obligated to someone

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל does not feed a wife from her absent husband's property for two reasons: he may have left her money, or told her to keep her earnings. Neither reason fits a יבם, so a יבמה whose יבם ran away is fed from his property.

phrases.english: Shmuel can say to you:
What should we worry about in this case?
If it is because of bundles [of money] —
his mind is not close to her;
if it is because of her earnings —
she is not bound to him.
phrases.notes: Her earnings do not belong to the יבם, so he could not have told her to live off them in place of support.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ שְׁמוּאֵל: לְמַאי נֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ לְהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא about the יבמה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the reasons behind the ruling do not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Feeding a יבמה from an absent יבם's property shows that we do not worry the absent man already arranged her support.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's worries come from the closeness and rights of a husband. A יבם would not leave her money and has no claim to her earnings, so the two cases are different.

steps.title: A woman returns from overseas and is fed from her husband's property
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a woman who comes back from overseas and says her husband died may choose to be fed or to collect her כתובה. If she says he divorced her, she is supported up to the amount of her כתובה. This seems to go against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A woman went overseas with her husband. She came back and said, 'My husband died.' If she wants, she is fed from his property. If she wants, she collects her כתובה. If she said, 'My husband divorced me,' she keeps being supported up to the amount of her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to show a wife is fed from her husband's property even though he is not here. That would go against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is not present, and nobody knows for sure what happened to him. Still, the ברייתא lets her take money from his property, either as food or as her כתובה. That looks like the opposite of שמואל, who does not feed a wife while her husband is away.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening for bringing a source as a proof or a challenge
Overseas, a faraway place
She is fed (supported from his property)
She collects the payment of her כתובה
She keeps on supporting herself, over time

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
phrases.english: A woman who went, she and her husband, overseas,
and she came back and said, "My husband died,"
if she wants, she is fed,
if she wants, she collects her marriage contract.
If she said, "My husband divorced me,"
she keeps supporting herself up to the amount of her marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the יבם case was answered, the גמרא brings another source against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that בית דין does not feed the wife of an absent husband
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives the woman food or her כתובה from the property of a husband who is not present. That suggests an absent husband's wife is fed.

steps.title: The case is when people heard that the husband died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא, like an earlier source, is talking about a case where a report came that the husband died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is talking about a case where they heard about him that he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by saying the ברייתא is about a husband who is reported dead, not just away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל only refuses to feed a wife whose husband is alive and away. If people heard he died, his property can be used to support her, so the ברייתא does not argue with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: the same answer as before
When they heard about him that he died

phrases.english: Here too,
it is when they heard about him that he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a husband who is simply away, so it argues with שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a husband reported dead, so it does not argue with שמואל.

steps.title: Why is she supported only up to her כתובה amount?
steps.stepSummary: If the husband is reported dead, why does the woman who claims divorce get food only up to the value of her כתובה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it different, that she gets only up to the amount of her כתובה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the new explanation. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow is normally fed from her husband's estate with no fixed limit. If the husband is reported dead, why should the woman who says she was divorced be limited to her כתובה amount?

keyTerms.meaning: And what is different? A request for the reason behind a difference
Up to the amount of her כתובה

phrases.english: And what is different, that it is only up to the amount of her marriage contract?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a detail of the ברייתא now that it is explained as a case where the husband is reported dead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a woman claiming divorce gets support capped at her כתובה, if her husband is reported dead.

steps.title: She caused the loss to herself
steps.stepSummary: By saying she was divorced, the woman herself gave up the endless support a widow gets.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because she is the one who caused the loss to herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Her own claim of divorce is what limits her support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A divorced woman gets her כתובה but no ongoing food. Since she herself claimed to be divorced, she loses the widow's right to food and gets only up to her כתובה amount.

keyTerms.meaning: She caused a loss to herself

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is explained as a case where the husband was reported dead, so it is no challenge to שמואל. The cap at her כתובה comes from her own claim of divorce.

phrases.english: Because she is the one who caused the loss to herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her own claim of divorce takes away her widow's right to food, so she is supported only up to her כתובה.

steps.title: A refusing girl loses food, so others whose husbands are away must get it
steps.stepSummary: A source explains that a ממאנת gets no food in a case where her husband went overseas and she borrowed money to eat. That suggests a girl who does not refuse would be fed, which goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: In what case did they say a girl who refuses her husband gets no food? You cannot say it is while she lives with her husband, because her husband must feed her. Rather, it is when her husband went overseas, and she borrowed money and ate, and then she refused him. The reason she gets nothing is that she refused. This shows that if she did not refuse, we give her food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another source against שמואל. It reads a lesson out of it: because she refused, she loses food. So without refusal, a wife whose husband is away would be fed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source places the case when the husband is overseas. It blames her loss only on her refusal. That suggests a normal wife whose husband is away gets food from his property, which is exactly what שמואל denies.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl married as a minor (by her mother or brothers) who refuses her husband and leaves without a גט
She borrowed money and ate (spent it on food)
The reason is: the start of reading a lesson from the wording
We give her (food)

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיצַד אָמְרוּ מְמָאֶנֶת אֵין לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת?
phrases.english: In what case did they say a girl who refuses gets no food?

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר בְּיוֹשֶׁבֶת תַּחַת בַּעְלָהּ —
phrases.english: You cannot say it is when she lives with her husband,
because her husband is obligated to feed her.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם,
phrases.english: Rather, it is when her husband went overseas,
and she borrowed and ate, and then she got up and refused him.
The reason is that she refused,
so if she did not refuse, we give her food!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כֵּיצַד אָמְרוּ מְמָאֶנֶת אֵין לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous ברייתא was answered, the גמרא brings a new source against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that בית דין does not feed the wife of an absent husband
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only refusal takes away her food, so a wife who does not refuse, whose husband is overseas, is fed from his property.

steps.title: שמואל: neither worry applies to a young girl
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that a minor is different. A husband would not leave a bundle of money with a young girl, and her earnings are not enough to feed her. So she is fed, but an adult wife is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל can say to you: What is there to worry about here? If the worry is a bundle of money he left her, nobody leaves a bundle of money with a minor. If the worry is that he told her to live on her earnings, a minor's earnings are not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. His two reasons for not feeding an absent husband's wife do not fit a young girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not feed an adult wife because he may have left her money or told her to live on her earnings. With a minor, both worries fall away, so feeding her teaches nothing about an adult wife.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you: introduces how someone would defend his view
What should we worry about for her?
A minor girl
He does not hand over (leave with her)
Is not enough

steps.whatToRemember: Each source brought against שמואל was answered. Either the husband was reported dead, or the case is special: a יבם, or a minor. In those cases his worries about hidden money or her earnings do not apply.

phrases.english: Shmuel can say to you:
Here, what should we worry about for her?
If it is because of bundles of money,
nobody hands bundles of money to a minor;
and if it is because of her earnings,
a minor's earnings are not enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ שְׁמוּאֵל: הָכָא לְמַאי נֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8, using the same two reasons שמואל gave in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the reasons behind the rule do not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Feeding a ממאנת who did not refuse shows that every wife whose husband is away is fed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A minor is fed only because שמואל's two worries do not apply to her. An adult wife is still not fed.

steps.title: What was decided in practice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final outcome was in the argument between רב and שמואל about giving food to a wife whose husband went away.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the conclusion about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by asking how the argument between רב and שמואל actually played out in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל has defended his view against the sources, but defending a view is not the same as deciding the הלכה. So the גמרא now looks for real court cases to see what judges actually did.

keyTerms.meaning: What happened with it? What was the outcome?
Food or support money

phrases.english: What was the conclusion about this?
phrases.notes: "This" means the argument between רב and שמואל about feeding a wife whose husband went overseas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After שמואל's defense in step 9, the גמרא moves from defending his view to asking for the practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How courts actually ruled when a wife whose husband went overseas asked for food.

steps.title: רב דימי reports two real cases
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי gave the woman food in בית שערים, while רבי ישמעאל refused in ציפורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: A case like this came before רבי in בית שערים, and he gave her food. A case came before רבי ישמעאל in ציפורי, and he did not give her food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question with real court cases. Two great judges ruled in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ruled like רב and gave her food. רבי ישמעאל ruled like שמואל and refused. So the answer is not simple, and the next step will ask about רבי ישמעאל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: When [a scholar] came from ארץ ישראל to בבל
A real case that happened
He ruled for her, set an amount for her

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי בְּבֵית שְׁעָרִים
phrases.english: A case came before Rabbi in Beit She'arim
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and he set food for her.
[A case came] before Rabbi Yishmael in Tzippori,
and he did not set food for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by reporting real cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי gave food (like רב). רבי ישמעאל did not (like שמואל).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן questions רבי ישמעאל's refusal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks why רבי ישמעאל refused food, since in the משנה חנן and the בני כהנים גדולים argue only about an oath and both agree she gets food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן wondered about this: What did רבי ישמעאל see that made him not give her food? After all, the sons of the High Priests and חנן argued only about an oath, but food we do give her!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges רבי ישמעאל's ruling by pointing to a משנה that seems to show the woman gets food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה about someone who fed the wife (steps 21–23), רבי יוחנן reads the argument between חנן and the בני כהנים גדולים as being only about the oath. That suggests both sides agree she receives food, which would support רב. So how could רבי ישמעאל refuse?

keyTerms.meaning: He wondered about it, was puzzled
The sons of the High Priests, judges quoted in the משנה
A judge who argues with the בני כהנים גדולים in the משנה
An oath
We give

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan wondered about it:
And what did Rabbi Yishmael see
that he did not set food for her?

phrases.aramaic: הָא לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בְּנֵי כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים וְחָנָן
phrases.english: After all, the sons of the High Priests and Chanan did not argue
phrases.notes: This is the משנה that comes up later on this amud (steps 21–23), about someone who fed a wife while her husband was overseas.

phrases.english: except about the oath,
but food, we give her!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּהֵי בַּהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְכִי מָה רָאָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רבי ישמעאל reported in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's refusal to give food (which matches שמואל's view).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's argument is only about the oath, so both sides must agree that food is given. That goes against refusing food.

steps.title: שמואל explained the משנה as a case where the husband was reported dead
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא answers that שמואל explained the משנה as talking about a husband who was reported dead. רבי יוחנן reacts with amazement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said to him: Our teacher שמואל in בבל already explained it as a case where they heard that the husband died. רבי יוחנן said to him: You have gone so far in working this out?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמן בר אבא defends רבי ישמעאל. The משנה is not about an ordinary husband who went away. It is about a husband who was reported dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband was reported dead, she is fed like a widow. So the משנה says nothing about a living husband who is simply away. That leaves room for רבי ישמעאל to rule like שמואל, and רבי יוחנן is amazed at how deeply they had learned the topic in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, read it as referring to
When they heard that he died
You have explained, solved

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's last line is not a new challenge. He is expressing amazement that the scholars in בבל had already solved his question.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said to him:
Our teacher Shmuel in Babylonia already explained it
as a case where they heard that he died.
He said to him:
You have explained it this much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the source (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about any husband who went overseas, so food is always given.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a husband reported dead, so it does not contradict refusing food when the husband is just away.

steps.title: רבין reports the same cases the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: רבין says the cases happened the other way around: רבי refused food and רבי ישמעאל gave it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: A case came before רבי in בית שערים, and he did not give her food. A case came before רבי ישמעאל in ציפורי, and he gave her food.
steps.whatsHappening: A second scholar tells a different version of the same reports. The judges' rulings are switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבין's version, רבי is the one who ruled like שמואל and refused food. The discussion that follows is the same, but now it is aimed at רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: A scholar who, like רב דימי, brought teachings from ארץ ישראל to בבל

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי בְּבֵית שְׁעָרִים,
phrases.english: A case came before Rabbi in Beit She'arim,
and he did not set food for her.
[A case came] before Rabbi Yishmael in Tzippori,
and he set food for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the report in step 11, with the rulings reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי refused food. רבי ישמעאל gave food.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן questions רבי's refusal
steps.stepSummary: In רבין's version, רבי יוחנן asks why רבי refused, using the same משנה about חנן and the בני כהנים גדולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: What did רבי see that made him not give her food? After all, חנן and the sons of the High Priests argued only about an oath, but food we do give her.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the same challenge as step 12. This time it is aimed at רבי, since in this version he is the one who refused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning has not changed: the משנה's argument is only about the oath, so it seems everyone agrees she gets food. Only the target of the question has switched.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he see? What was his reason?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מָה רָאָה רַבִּי שֶׁלֹּא פָּסַק לָהּ?
phrases.english: What did Rabbi see that he did not set [food] for her?

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ חָנָן וּבְנֵי כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים
phrases.english: For Chanan and the sons of the High Priests did not argue
except about the oath,
but food, we give her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מָה רָאָה רַבִּי שֶׁלֹּא פָּסַק לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's refusal as reported in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's refusal to give food in רבין's version.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה argues only about the oath, which suggests food is given.

steps.title: The same answer: the משנה is about a husband reported dead
steps.stepSummary: רב שמן בר אבא again answers with שמואל's explanation, and רבי יוחנן again reacts with amazement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמן בר אבא said to him: שמואל in בבל already explained it as a case where they heard the husband died. רבי יוחנן said to him: You have gone so far in working this out?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is the same as in step 13. This time it defends רבי's refusal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה is about a husband reported dead, it gives no proof for feeding the wife of a living husband who went away. Both versions end with the same exchange.

keyTerms.meaning: Already

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shemen bar Abba said to him:
Shmuel in Babylonia already explained it
as a case where they heard that he died.
He said to him:
You have explained it this much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 the same way step 13 answered step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the source (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה proves food is given to the wife of any husband who is away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a husband reported dead, so refusing food is still possible.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב: we give food to a married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב: a בית דין gives food to a married woman whose husband went away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like רב, and we give food to a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the whole argument: we follow רב, not שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though שמואל's view was defended all along, the practical ruling is that a בית דין gives food to the wife of a husband who went overseas.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is like him
We set, we rule [an amount]
A married woman

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: like רב, a בית דין gives food to a married woman whose husband went away.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל's answers were defended successfully, but that does not mean the הלכה follows him. Here it follows רב.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Rav,
and we set food for a married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question from step 10 after both reports.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We give food to a married woman whose husband went away, like רב.

steps.title: A wife may give up her food in exchange for keeping her earnings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא also rules like רב הונא in the name of רב: a wife can tell her husband she won't take food from him and won't give him her earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like what רב הונא said in the name of רב. For רב הונא said in the name of רב: A woman can say to her husband, 'I will not be fed by you, and I will not work for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second related ruling about a wife's food: she may choose to give it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the husband feeds his wife and receives what she earns from her work. This ruling says the wife can cancel that deal: she gives up her food and keeps her earnings for herself.

keyTerms.meaning: She is able, she may
I will not be fed [by you]
I will not work [for you]

steps.whatToRemember: A wife may give up her right to food from her husband and keep her own earnings.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב.
phrases.english: And the halacha is like Rav Huna said in the name of Rav.
For Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
A woman may say to her husband
"I will not be fed and I will not work."
phrases.notes: "I will not work" means her earnings stay hers and don't go to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling about a wife's food right after the main ruling in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A wife may refuse food from her husband and keep her earnings.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב זביד on glazed vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רב זביד: white and black glazed vessels are permitted, and green ones are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows רב זביד about glazed vessels. He said: white and black glazed vessels are permitted, and green ones are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more final ruling to its list. This time it is about clay vessels that have a glaze coating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain clay soaks up whatever is cooked or stored in it, so a clay vessel that once held forbidden food stays forbidden. רב זביד teaches that white and black glaze seals the clay, so those vessels can be used again. Green glaze does not seal it, so green vessels stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is (the practical ruling)
A glaze coating on clay vessels
White ones and black ones
Green ones
Permitted / forbidden

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Rav Zevid regarding glazed vessels.
phrases.notes: קוניא is the shiny coating painted onto clay pots.

phrases.english: As Rav Zevid said:
These glazed vessels:
the white and black ones are permitted.
phrases.notes: Once they are washed, they can be used again even if forbidden food was in them.

phrases.english: The green ones are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of final rulings from steps 17 and 18 with an unrelated topic.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: White and black glazed vessels are permitted after washing. Green glazed vessels are forbidden.

steps.title: Cracked glazed vessels are always forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The permission for white and black vessels applies only when they have no cracks. Cracked ones are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said white and black vessels are permitted when they have no cracks. If they have cracks, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a limit on the ruling it just gave about white and black vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The glaze helps only if it fully seals the clay. Where there are cracks, food soaks into the clay underneath, so the vessel goes back to being forbidden, like plain clay.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when (a phrase that sets a limit)
Cracks

phrases.english: And we only said this
when they have no cracks,
but if they have cracks, they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵית בְּהוּ קַרְטוּפָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on step 19's permission for white and black vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: White and black glazed vessels are permitted only if they have no cracks. Cracked ones are forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Glazed vessels: white and black are permitted, green are forbidden, and any vessel with cracks is forbidden.

steps.title: New משנה: someone supports a wife while her husband is overseas
steps.stepSummary: A husband goes overseas and someone else supports his wife. חנן says the provider has lost his money.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man went overseas, and someone else supported his wife. חנן says: the provider lost his money.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a provider who pays for a wife's food while her husband is away, and gives חנן's view that the provider cannot collect from the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband never asked this person to support his wife. So חנן holds the husband does not have to pay him back, and the money is simply lost.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Overseas, a faraway land
Supported, provided food for
He lost his money

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same משנה רבי יוחנן cited in steps 12 and 15. He read the argument here as being only about the oath, with both sides agreeing that the wife herself is given food.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who went overseas,
and someone arose and supported his wife,
Chanan says: he has lost his money.
phrases.notes: "He" is the provider. He cannot collect from the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the list of final rulings ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חנן, someone who supports another man's wife without being asked cannot get his money back from the husband.

steps.title: The בני כהנים גדולים disagree, and רבי דוסא agrees with them
steps.stepSummary: The בני כהנים גדולים say the provider swears how much he spent and collects it. רבי דוסא בן הרכינס agrees with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בני כהנים גדולים disagreed with him and said: he swears how much he spent and takes it. רבי דוסא בן הרכינס said: the הלכה is like them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the opposite opinion to חנן's: the provider can collect from the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בני כהנים גדולים hold that the husband must repay what was spent on his wife. Since the husband cannot know the exact amount, the provider takes an oath about how much he spent. רבי דוסא בן הרכינס adds his support to their view.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of the High Priests
He swears (takes an oath)
And he takes (collects)
Like their words, in agreement with them

phrases.english: The sons of the High Priests disagreed with him
and said: he swears how much he spent, and takes it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסָא בֶּן הַרְכִּינָס כְּדִבְרֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa ben Harkinas said: it is like their words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opinion opposed to חנן's ruling in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The provider swears how much he spent and collects it from the husband.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי sides with חנן
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says חנן is right: the provider put his money where it cannot be recovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said: חנן spoke well. The provider put his money on a deer's horn.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי backing חנן's opinion, using a picture to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money placed on the horn of a running deer is gone. It runs away and you have no realistic way to get it back. In the same way, someone who spends money without the husband's instruction has no real claim to be repaid.

keyTerms.meaning: He spoke well, he is right
The horn of a deer, a picture for money that cannot be recovered

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two sides. חנן and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי say the provider loses his money. The בני כהנים גדולים and רבי דוסא בן הרכינס say he swears how much he spent and collects it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai said:
Chanan spoke well;
he placed his money on the horn of a deer.
phrases.notes: Picture a deer running off with your money on its horn. You are not getting it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי: יָפֶה אָמַר חָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to support חנן's view from step 21, against step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנן is correct: the provider has no claim against the husband.

steps.title: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה about a vow forbidding benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by citing a משנה from another place about a person who is forbidden by a vow from benefiting from his friend.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: someone who is forbidden by a vow from getting benefit from his friend...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its discussion by quoting a משנה from a different מסכת. This is a setup line: the quote continues on the next amud, and the גמרא will then connect it to our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה dealt with someone who pays to support a woman without the husband asking him to. The גמרא brings a case of מודר הנאה, where one person may not benefit from another. The question of whether paying someone's debts or needs counts as 'giving him benefit' will link the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
"We learned there": a quote from a משנה in a different place in ש״ס
A person forbidden by a נדר from getting any benefit from someone
From his friend (the other person in the vow)

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is not finished here. Don't look for the ruling yet; the rest of the משנה from נדרים comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" means a משנה in a different מסכת, here in נדרים.

phrases.english: One who is forbidden by a vow from benefiting from his friend —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה of steps 21-23 by bringing in a parallel משנה about מודר הנאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the case of a person who is מודר הנאה from his friend; the ruling comes in the continuation of the quote.
